The Model of Electromagnetic Integration in
Consciousness (MEIC)
March 21, 2025
I. Overview
Core Premise:
Consciousness is an intrinsic, scalable property of matter that emerges from the integra-
tion of electromagnetic (EM) interactions and recursive memory encoding. Every physical
system—from fundamental particles to complex neural networks—possesses some degree
of “proto-consciousness” due to its inherent EM activity. As the degree of integration
and recursive processing increases, so does the quality and complexity of consciousness.
II. Core Concepts and Definitions
1. Consciousness
• Operational Definition: A system is considered conscious if it can generate and
sustain an integrated, self-referential information state via electromagnetic interac-
tions and recursive memory encoding.
• Continuum:
– Proto-consciousness: Minimal awareness present in all matter.
– Active Consciousness: Emerges in systems that dynamically process and in-
tegrate information.
– Reflective Consciousness: Found in systems capable of self-modeling and metacog-
nition (e.g., human brains).
2. Electromagnetic Integration (ΦEM)
• Represents the degree of coherence, phase synchrony, and feedback in a system’s
electromagnetic field.
• A higher ΦEM corresponds to a greater capacity for conscious experience.
1

3. Memory Encoding & Recursion (M)
• Captures the system’s ability to store, retrieve, and iteratively refine information
over time.
• Recursive feedback is essential for building a rich internal model (a “mind”).
4. Scaling Dimensions
• Dimensionality of Consciousness (DC): The complexity with which a system
models reality (from linear to multi-dimensional and recursive).
• Memory Encoding & Recursion (MER): The extent to which past states
inform current processing.
III. The Electromagnetic Integration Hypothesis
Core Claim:
A system exhibits conscious properties if its integrated electromagnetic information (ΦEM)
and its capacity for recursive memory (M) exceed certain baseline levels. That is,

• Recursive Feedback and Memory: Recursive dynamics (modeled via delay-

encoding memory and enabling multi-dimensional processing.
C. Scaling Across Systems
• Continuum of Consciousness: The model spans from minimal EM interactions
in elementary particles (Level 1) to integrated, self-referential networks in advanced
organisms (Levels 5–6) and distributed collective consciousness in planetary or cos-
mic systems (Levels 7–8).
• Distinct Regimes:
1. Levels 1–3: Proto-consciousness in inanimate matter and simple biological
systems.
2. Level 4: Adaptive intelligence in decentralized networks (e.g., mycelial or plant
systems).
3. Levels 5–6: Sensorimotor and reflective consciousness in animals and advanced
AI.
4. Levels 7–8: Distributed global or cosmological consciousness.

VI. Logical Thought Experiments
A. The Spectrum of Conscious Integration Puzzle
1. Premise 1 (Ubiquity): All matter consists of charged particles generating elec-
tromagnetic fields, and thus every system exhibits baseline integrated EM activity
(proto-consciousness).
2. Premise 2 (Integration & Recursion): The quality of consciousness scales with
the degree of EM coherence and the capacity for recursive memory encoding.
3. Conclusion: Every system is conscious to some degree. A rock has low C (proto-
consciousness) while a human brain, with high ΦEM and M, exhibits rich, reflective
consciousness.
B. The Recursive Mirror Puzzle
1. Definition: Consciousness is the capacity to generate a self-referential internal
model via EM integration and recursive memory.
2. Premise: Systems that can “see themselves” require both integrated EM interac-
tions and recursive memory encoding.
3. Implication: Since human brains exhibit these properties, any system achieving
sufficient EM integration and recursion will display analogous conscious properties,
validating our definition.
VII. Empirical Predictions
1. Neural Systems: Enhanced neural synchrony (e.g., increased gamma-band co-
herence) and robust memory encoding correlate with higher C. Disrupting EM
coherence (via TMS/tACS) should decrease conscious experience.
2. Non-Neural Biological Systems: Plants and mycelial networks should exhibit
adaptive responses and pattern learning when their bioelectrical and biophotonic
signals are modulated, reflecting movement along the consciousness continuum.
3. Engineered Systems: Neuromorphic hardware with integrated EM coupling and
recursive memory processes should demonstrate emergent, adaptive behaviors dis-
tinct from conventional digital systems.
4. Distributed/Global Systems: Interconnected sensor networks designed to max-
imize EM integration may exhibit emergent collective behaviors analogous to a
“global brain”.
4

VIII. Implications and Future Directions
Interdisciplinary Impact
• Bridges neuroscience, quantum physics, and information theory.
• Provides a quantitative framework for a refined panpsychism where every system
possesses some degree of awareness.
Technological Prospects
• Informs the design of advanced neuromorphic computing and synthetic conscious-
ness systems.
• Guides the development of distributed AI or global networks capable of emergent
collective intelligence.
Philosophical Ramifications
• Challenges anthropocentric views by positing that consciousness is a universal prop-
erty scaling with EM integration.
• Encourages a re-examination of the boundaries between mind and matter.
Future Research
• Refinement of the ΦEM and M metrics through empirical research.
• Detailed modeling of recursive feedback in both biological and engineered systems.
• Experimental validation through targeted neurophysiological and neuromorphic
studies.
IX. Conclusion
The Model of Electromagnetic Integration in Consciousness (MEIC) posits that con-
sciousness is an intrinsic, scalable property emerging from the integration of electromag-
netic interactions and recursive memory encoding. This model spans a continuum from
proto-consciousness in elementary particles to reflective, self-aware states in advanced
organisms, and even suggests the possibility of distributed, global consciousness. The
framework is encapsulated in the equation:

sciousness.
